Provide estimates of hour and cost burdens of the collection of information.

TSA uses historical data from the LEO Flying Armed Application which vets and stores all National Law Enforcement Telecommunications System messages (known as flying while armed messages) submitted by state, local, and tribal LEOs.  Based on this data, TSA estimates an average annual number of 83,749 responses to this collection.  Each response consists of filling out a short form at the screening checkpoint.  TSA estimates that the time burden for this activity is 4 minute (0.0667 hours).  TSA estimates the average annual hour burden cost to the public to be 5,583 hours per year (16,750 hours over the 3-year period).  Respondents to this collection are state, local, tribal, and territorial LEOs travelling on official business, therefore TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage rate of $64.48 to estimate the hour burden cost.  TSA estimates the average annual hour burden cost to the public to be $359,990.  Table 1 summarizes these calculations.
There are no capital or start-up costs associated with this collection.

Provide estimates of annualized cost to the Federal Government.  Also, provide a description of the method used to estimate cost, and other expenses that would not have been incurred without this collection of information.

TSA airport screening personnel monitor, transport, and store completed checkpoint log-in forms.  TSA estimates it takes a Supervisory Transportation Security Officer approximately 1.5 minutes (0.025 hours) to monitor, transport, and store forms per LEO checking-in for their pre-flight screening.  TSA estimates an average annual hour burden of 2,094 hours (6,281 of the 3-year window).  A Supervisory Transportation Security Officer has a fully-loaded wage rate of $75.94.  TSA estimates an average annual hour burden cost to TSA of $158,997 ($476,991 over 3 years).  This collection does not involve other federal entities; therefore, the TSA cost is the federal cost.  Table 2 summarizes these calculations.
